note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 by an independent auditor after the userns conversion. The unit's only change since the last verdict is userns.Enter(t) as its first statement (the child re-runs the whole body in its own user, network and mount namespace; a child failure or skip propagates to the parent, and a child that ran nothing fails it) plus removal of EPERM/EACCES skips, so a refused privilege now fails instead of skipping. Assertions are byte-identical. Section 3.11.5: 'RSVP must be able to cause Path, PathTear, and ResvConf message to be sent with the Router Alert IP option.' TestIntegrationRSVPPathCarriage sends PATH, PathTear and a ResvConf through production SendPath and rsvpWireAssertIP fails unless the captured IPv4 options are exactly 94040000; the Send control on link 1 must carry no options, so the alert is bound to SendPath. Negatives unchanged: TestRFC2205PathNeverLeavesWithoutRouterAlertCarrier and TestRFC2205ResvConfNeverLeavesWithoutRouterAlertCarrier.
